_comment: Cheap bulk-evaluation listener: openai/gpt-oss-120b on DeepInfra, an open-weight 120B model at $0.037/$0.17 per 1M tokens -- measured at 47x cheaper per call than Sonnet 5 at effort=medium on this workload ($0.000102 vs $0.00477; see codenames/guessers/openai_compat.py). NOT the frozen eval suite: that is configs/guesser_pool_llm_sonnet.json and evaluation results still come only from there (docs/iteration-architecture.md's 'two roles for guessers'). This pool exists so a sigma sweep can afford enough games to resolve differences that a per-turn proxy gets wrong -- see docs/log.md on sigma=1.5 vs 2.5. reasoning_effort is low, and must be set explicitly: gpt-oss-120b reasons by default at medium, which costs 8x the completion tokens for the same one-shot associative judgment and -- on a small max_tokens -- returns an empty answer that the tolerant parser would turn into a fabricated board-order ranking. Cache keys are namespaced provider/model, so these rankings share cache/llm_store.db with the Anthropic ones without colliding.
